Latin word

apparō

apparō, apparāre, apparāvī, apparātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive · Conjugation on Wiktionary

organise, get up (a dinner, a wedding, games); prepare with care (a meal, a wedding)

In this lexicon

  • organise

    the recommended word · classical · Ter. Ad. 966: apparāre dē diē convīvium; Cic. Q. fr. 3.8 (Lewis & Short): lūdōs magnificentissimōs

  • prepare

    also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 901: in apparandō cōnsūmunt diem; Ter. Ad. 966: apparāre dē diē convīvium

Examples

  • Occīdunt mē quidem dum nimis sānctās nūptiās student facere: in apparandō cōnsūmunt diem.

    They’re killing me, wanting to make the wedding too perfect: they’re spending the whole day on the arrangements.Ter. Ad. 900–901

    In the entry for organise

  • sī bellī homunculī conlēctī sunt, sī ēlēctus locus, sī tempus lēctum, sī apparātus nōn neglēctus

    if nice people have been brought together, if the place has been chosen, the time picked, and the preparations not neglectedGell. 13.11.3 (Varro)
